original_task.problem:
Let X be a connected compact complex manifold of dimension n, and use dd^c=(i/(2 pi)) partial barpartial. A smooth real (1,1)-background theta need not be closed. PSH(X,theta) consists of genuine quasi-plurisubharmonic u with theta+dd^c u>=0. Write v preceq u if v<=u+C for some constant C; ordinary equivalence means bounded difference. The multiplier ideal I(tu) consists of germs g for which |g|^2 exp(-tu) is locally integrable. Write v preceq_I u if I(tv) is contained in I(tu) for every real t>0. For a smooth real obstacle F define P_{theta,F}[u]=(sup{v in PSH(X,theta):v<=F, v preceq u})^* and P_{theta,F}[u]_I=(sup{v in PSH(X,theta):v<=F, v preceq_I u})^*, where * is upper semicontinuous regularization. Omitting F means F=0. For a positive Hermitian form h, bounded mass (BMP) means the supremum of integral_X(h+dd^c v)^n over bounded h-psh v is finite. The extended non-pluripolar measure MA_theta^ext(v) is the increasing finite-level product, which may have infinite total mass. The lower singularity volume of an ordinary type q is inf{MA_theta^ext(v)(X):v in PSH(X,theta),v equivalent to q}. The relative envelope class E_env(X,theta,q) consists of u preceq q such that for every b>=1 some v in PSH(X,theta) satisfies b^(-1)v+(1-b^(-1))q<=u; this uses convex sums even at common poles.

Question: suppose the smooth background theta is admissible for these envelope constructions, u belongs to PSH(X,theta), and P_theta[u]=P_theta[u]_I is genuine. Must P_{theta,F}[u]=P_{theta,F}[u]_I for every smooth real obstacle F, without positive lower ideal volume or BMP? Establish the implication in unrestricted higher-dimensional zero-volume and unbounded-mass settings, or give a counterexample. All-obstacle equality implies zero-obstacle equality by F=0. The converse is known when u belongs to E_env(X,theta,P_theta[u]_I), under BMP plus positive lower volume of the ideal envelope, on curves without volume restrictions, and in specified separated-product and divisorial-curve-fibration cases. These are background rather than resolutions of the unrestricted question. Smooth-gauge transport is also background.
original_task.completionCriteria: Prove the universal implication with all original hypotheses and without adding BMP or positive lower volume, or exhibit a compact complex manifold, explicit admissible smooth background theta, a genuine theta-psh u and a smooth obstacle F with rigorously proved zero-obstacle envelope equality and rigorously proved unequal obstacle envelopes. Expand any further admissibility used. A restricted example, a theorem repeating the known relative-envelope criterion, or gauge transport alone cannot resolve the question. Check all external premises against primary sources and reconstruct the complete proof independently.

notes.summary: S09 was not settled by this bounded investigation: neither the unrestricted implication nor a qualifying counterexample was established.
notes.detailedSummary: The inspected sources leave an ordinary obstacle-transport step unsupported on arbitrary nonclosed backgrounds at zero lower volume and without BMP. A July 2026 preprint updates zero-mass idempotence in closed big classes, but does not supply the requested universal theorem. No relative-envelope membership is inferred from zero-obstacle equality.
notes.text:
This literature investigation did not establish the universal implication and did not find a counterexample satisfying both the zero-obstacle equality and the obstacle inequality. This is a bounded search conclusion, not a claim that no theorem or counterexample exists.

The concrete remaining target is ordinary obstacle transport. Normalize u≤0, put q=Pθ[u]=Pθ[u]I, and consider the finite rooftops qC=Pθ(min{u+C,0}), increasing to q after regularization. For a θ-psh w ordinarily equivalent to q and satisfying w≤F, investigate whether (limC→∞ Pθ(min{qC,w}))*=w under the original admissibility alone. Such a statement would address approximation by potentials constrained by the original ordinary type of u. Equality of singularity types, ideal preservation, and zero-obstacle idempotence do not themselves prove this limit identity. Alternatively, seek an actual failure of this approximation and then verify the multiplier-ideal antecedent independently.

Primary full texts inspected included Darvas–Xia’s two requested papers, the domination principle they invoke, Boucksom–Guedj–Lu, Alehyane–Lu–Salouf, Xuan Li, and the July 2026 Pang–Sun–Wang–Zhou preprint. No proof of the universal claim is inferred from these readings.

Retrieval limitation: opening the [publisher’s Alehyane–Lu–Salouf article](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022123626002727) returned an internal error. Its [arXiv v1 full text](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.02339v1) was successfully inspected; differences in the publisher version remain unchecked.

notes.summary: Darvas–Xia Proposition 5.8 proves ordinary obstacle transport with positive mass on closed pseudoeffective backgrounds over compact Kähler manifolds.
notes.detailedSummary: Section 5 requires X compact connected Kähler, θ smooth closed real and pseudoeffective, K closed nonpluripolar, and a continuous obstacle on K. Proposition 5.8 additionally requires positive mass of u. Its domination argument does not cover zero mass.
notes.text:
Inspected [arXiv:2112.03827v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2112.03827v4), Section 5, printed pp. 19–22. Proposition 5.8 requires u to “be a potential with positive mass” and states PK[u](v)=PK[P[u]](v), followed by PK[u](v)=PK[PK[u](v)](v). The published text retains this hypothesis: [Geometry & Topology, pp. 1981–1982](https://research.chalmers.se/publication/542539/file/542539_Fulltext.pdf).

Proof: set A=PK[u](v), B=PK[P[u]](v). Lemma 5.2 gives equivalent ordinary singularities. Equation (26) gives A=PK[Vθ](v)=v almost everywhere for MAθ(A). Since A≤B≤PK[Vθ](v), A=B there. The cited domination principle gives A≥B everywhere, hence equality. Lemma 5.2 then supplies the final idempotence identity.

At zero mass, this almost-everywhere comparison is vacuous. Lemma 5.2’s unrestricted bounded-difference statements and Corollary 5.3’s ideal-envelope idempotence do not remove that obstruction.

notes.summary: The closures paper uses ideal inclusion for every real exponent; ideal preservation and idempotence do not transport the ordinary envelope of u.
notes.detailedSummary: In the closed pseudoeffective Kähler setting, equation (2.19) identifies inclusion-defined and equality-defined ideal envelopes. Proposition 2.18 preserves every multiplier ideal and makes the ideal envelope both ordinary model and ideal model. The recorded counterexample fails S09’s antecedent.
notes.text:
Inspected [Darvas–Xia, The closures of test configurations and algebraic singularity types](https://research.chalmers.se/publication/528300/file/528300_Fulltext.pdf), Section 2.4, pp. 19–24. Definition 2.12 specifies inclusion “for all a > 0”; these are real-exponent tests.

Equation (2.19) identifies inclusion and equality candidate envelopes by replacing ψ with max{ψ,ϕ−supXϕ}. Proposition 2.18 states I(aP[ϕ]I)=I(aϕ), P[P[ϕ]I]I=P[ϕ]I, and P[P[ϕ]I]=P[ϕ]I, without a positive-mass hypothesis. Its proof uses increasing approximations and strong openness. These statements concern the ideal projection, not obstacle transport of the original ordinary constraint.

Example 2.19 records a potential on P¹ with P[v]I=0 but P[v]≠0. Consequently it fails the required zero-obstacle equality and is not an S09 counterexample.

Proposition 2.20 handles analytic singularity types. Theorem 2.24’s approximation characterization explicitly assumes positive mass; it supplies no unrestricted zero-volume transport theorem.

notes.summary: The exact domination principle used in Proposition 5.8 requires positive mass; its source explicitly identifies that condition as necessary.
notes.detailedSummary: Darvas–Di Nezza–Lu Corollary 3.10 assumes compact Kähler geometry, a smooth closed big background, u less singular than v, and positive mass of u. Almost-everywhere domination for MAθ(u) then implies pointwise domination.
notes.text:
Inspected [Darvas–Di Nezza–Lu, arXiv:1705.05796v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1705.05796v3), Corollary 3.10, printed p. 14. Under the paper’s compact Kähler, smooth closed big-background hypotheses, if u is less singular than v, ∫Xθuⁿ>0, and u≥v almost everywhere for θuⁿ, then u≥v on X. Immediately afterward the authors write that the non-collapsing mass condition is “trivially seen to be necessary.”

Thus Proposition 5.8’s invocation cannot simply be extended to a zero measure. Indeed, for any zero-mass potential a, taking b=a+1 makes a≥b almost everywhere for MAθ(a)=0 vacuous while pointwise domination fails. This diagnoses the proof obstruction; it is not a counterexample to S09.

notes.summary: Boucksom–Guedj–Lu supplies nonclosed envelope contact results, with BMP or specified local boundedness; it supplies no ordinary singularity transport theorem.
notes.detailedSummary: The inspected full text imposes BMP for its general finite nonpluripolar products. Its envelope section assumes a big background admitting an analytic-singularity strictly positive potential. Remark 2.10 removes BMP for measures locally bounded on the associated Zariski open set, not for arbitrary singular potentials.
notes.text:
Inspected [Boucksom–Guedj–Lu, Volumes of Bott–Chern classes, arXiv:2406.01090v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.01090v1). Theorem A and Section 2’s general product construction require BMP; the introduction says they “critically assume that X has the bounded mass property.”

Section 2.4 fixes a big background: there is ρ with analytic singularities and θ+ddcρ≥ωX, after scaling the Hermitian form. On Ω={ρ>−∞}, Theorem 2.9 states that a genuine envelope of a quasi-continuous obstacle has no Monge–Ampère mass below the obstacle.

Remark 2.10 explains that when the envelope is locally bounded on Ω, its measure can be understood there without BMP. This exception must not be expanded into a theorem about arbitrary unbounded envelopes with possibly infinite extended mass.

The inspected statements concern contact support and volume properties. They do not establish Pθ,F[u]=Pθ,F[Pθ[u]] in the unrestricted setting.

notes.summary: Alehyane–Lu–Salouf removes BMP in some Hermitian results, but its envelope characterization has additional model, finite-mass, and lower-volume hypotheses.
notes.detailedSummary: The background is semipositive and big. Their model definition additionally requires feasibility for a smaller background εθ. Theorem 5.11 requires finite mass of u and inherits v−(θ)>0 from Section 5.2. These conditions cannot be inferred from S09’s zero equality.
notes.text:
Inspected [Alehyane–Lu–Salouf, arXiv:2511.02339v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.02339v1), Sections 2.3, 3.1 and 5.2. Throughout, θ is semipositive and big; BMP is not globally assumed.

Definition 2.13 requires Pθ[ϕ]=ϕ and Pεθ(ϕ)≠−∞ for some ε∈(0,1). The latter means that a genuine εθ-psh function lies below ϕ, an additional feasibility condition. Definition 3.2 uses genuine envelopes Pθ(bu−(b−1)ϕ) for every b≥1 to define relative full mass.

Section 5.2 explicitly adds “the hypothesis v−(θ) > 0.” With its fixed model ϕ, Theorem 5.11 states that finite-mass u belongs to that relative class iff Pθ[u]=ϕ. Its reverse proof obtains positive lower singularity volume and invokes Proposition 3.4.

This does not authorize deducing the task’s relative-envelope antecedent from zero equality on arbitrary backgrounds, particularly for infinite-mass u or an ideal envelope lacking the smaller-background feasibility condition.

notes.summary: Xuan Li’s 2026 nonclosed model-envelope extension retains BMP and positive lower-volume assumptions.
notes.detailedSummary: The paper globally assumes finite upper and positive lower volume of a Hermitian metric. Its background is big in the analytic strictly positive sense. Proposition 3.4’s ordinary idempotence assumes positive lower volume of Pθ[u], excluding the relevant unrestricted zero-volume case.
notes.text:
Inspected [Xuan Li, arXiv:2601.13446v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.13446v1), introduction and Section 3. The introduction globally assumes the “bounded mass property as well as the positive volume property”: upper volume of ωX is finite and lower volume is positive.

Definition 2.1 calls θ big when an analytic-singularity θ-psh ρ satisfies θ+ddcρ≥δωX for δ>0. Proposition 3.4 assumes lower volume of Pθ[u] is positive and concludes Pθ[Pθ[u]]=Pθ[u]. Its proof invokes a domination principle. Proposition 3.1’s convex-subbarrier construction explicitly uses BMP to control its error term.

These are restricted nonclosed extensions, not an unrestricted S09 implication. Searches within the inspected PDF found no multiplier-ideal discussion, so no ideal-to-ordinary obstacle transport theorem was identified there.

notes.detailedSummary: Pang–Sun–Wang–Zhou states arbitrary-mass idempotence and a mixed-mass characterization on compact Kähler manifolds with closed big backgrounds. These remain ordinary unverified source claims here. No nonclosed extension is established.
notes.text:
Inspected [Pang–Sun–Wang–Zhou, arXiv:2607.12797v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.12797v1), July 14, 2026. Theorem 5.1, pp. 37–42, assumes compact Kähler X and smooth closed big θ and states Cθ(u)=Pθ[u] and Pθ[Pθ[u]]=Pθ[u] for every θ-psh u, including zero mass. Proposition 5.1 characterizes equality of ordinary envelopes for u≼ϕ by equality of all mixed masses ∫Xθuᵏ∧θVθⁿ⁻ᵏ=∫Xθϕᵏ∧θVθⁿ⁻ᵏ, k=0,…,n.

These preprint claims update older positive-mass idempotence results; no independent reconstruction or nonclosed application is asserted here.

A relevant mismatch: Theorem 8.1 states ideal-envelope capacity continuity without requiring positive limiting mass. Its proof, p. 52, invokes Lemma 3.1 for W. That lemma, p. 15, requires ∫XθWⁿ>0. The missing applicability justification prevents treating this proof as an unrestricted zero-mass result; it does not prove the theorem false.

# S09 reduction to ordinary-envelope idempotence along smooth gauges

- Result ID: S09-smooth-gauge-idempotence-reduction-20261013.draft
- Question: ../questions/Q001.md; ../references/S09-original-task.json
- Status: draft (conditional proof; pivotal general assumptions not independently certified)
- Date: 2026-10-13
- Origin: root mathematical exploration, alongside the native exact-S09 source run
- Verification: none for original S09; no original closure and no new delivered article
- Prior source check: ../verification/S09-primary-weighted-model-transport-scope-20261013.json

## Conditional statement, preserving the actual original order

Use D=i partial barpartial/(2 pi) and ideal INCLUSION at every real t>0.
Assume the relevant envelopes are genuine canonical theta-psh functions,
and assume the ideal envelope R_F=P_{theta,F}[u]_I satisfies
I(t R_F) subset I(tu) for every real t>0. This last preservation property
is explicitly an antecedent of this draft, not proved by an unsupported
limit passage. Assume P_theta[u]=P_theta[u]_I=q.

For a fixed smooth real F, set theta_F=theta+D F and u_F=u-F.
Then all-obstacle equality at this F is equivalent to the following
ordinary idempotence assertion at the smoothly transported input:

    P_{theta_F}[P_{theta_F}[u_F]]=P_{theta_F}[u_F].

If this idempotence holds for every smooth F (under the stated preservation
antecedents), the original all-obstacle conclusion follows. It does NOT
follow merely from idempotence at the single original zero obstacle.

## Complete conditional argument

Let Q_F=P_{theta,F}[u] and R_F=P_{theta,F}[u]_I, m=min F, M=max F.
Translation of competitors and zero-obstacle equality give

    q+m <= Q_F <= q+M,
    q+m <= R_F <= q+M.

Also Q_F<=R_F, because ordinary order implies the original ideal-inclusion
order: v<=u+C gives exp(-tv)>=exp(-tC)exp(-tu), so local integrability
for v implies that for u. In particular

    Q_F <= R_F <= Q_F+(M-m).

These are inequalities of extended real canonical functions; no subtraction
of infinities is needed. Thus Q_F and R_F have the same ordinary singularity
type. Smooth F also preserves ordinary and ideal orders. Directly changing
variables in the entire competitor families gives

    Q_F-F = P_{theta_F}[u-F],
    R_F-F = P_{theta_F}[u-F]_I.

Indeed theta_F+D(v-F)=theta+Dv, and v<=F is precisely v-F<=0.

Put q_F=Q_F-F and r_F=R_F-F. We show that r_F is an ORDINARY model for
theta_F. If w is theta_F-psh, w<=0 and w<=r_F+C, then w+F is theta-psh,
below F, and w+F<=R_F+C. Therefore

    I(t(w+F)) subset I(t R_F) subset I(tu)

for every real t>0, by the explicit preservation antecedent. Hence w+F
is an admissible ideal competitor for R_F and w<=r_F. Taking the upper
regularized supremum gives P_{theta_F}[r_F]<=r_F. Conversely r_F itself
is an ordinary competitor below zero, since R_F<=F. Thus

    P_{theta_F}[r_F]=r_F.

An ordinary envelope depends only on its input's ordinary singularity
type: adding a finite bound in either direction leaves its competitor
family unchanged. Since q_F and r_F have the same ordinary type,

    P_{theta_F}[q_F]=P_{theta_F}[r_F]=r_F.

It follows that P_{theta_F}[q_F]=q_F if and only if q_F=r_F, which is
exactly Q_F=R_F. This proves the claimed equivalence at the fixed F.
No Monge-Ampere product, total mass, BMP or positive lower volume was
used in this CONDITIONAL elementary proof.

## New primary lead and its exact limit

Opened Pang–Sun–Wang–Zhou, *Capacity Stability of Complex Monge-Ampere
Equations with Moving Prescribed Singularities*, arXiv:2607.12797v1,
14 July 2026. Theorem1.2/5.1 claims ordinary-envelope idempotence at
arbitrary mass for compact Kahler X and a CLOSED smooth real form in a
BIG cohomology class. Smooth gauge theta+D F retains that closed big
class, so this is a relevant candidate premise for a restricted zero-mass
application of the above reduction. It has NOT been admitted as a new
verified premise or as the unrestricted original theorem here.

The entire supplied Section5 proof was read in root native-web receipt
turn649934view0 (HTML lines1536–1760). It uses mixed non-pluripolar mass
preservation, positive-mass relative solvability, comparison, contact
support, and normalized tail estimates. Those supporting primary results
have NOT been independently reconstructed in this continuation. The proof
cannot be transported to arbitrary nonclosed forms or infinite masses by
just replacing the Kahler reference with a Hermitian one.

This is newly saved mathematical exploration and a bounded source lead;
it is not a new accepted full S09 solution. A general proof would need
idempotence on the required gauge orbit (or another route) and a fully
justified ideal-envelope preservation theorem at the stated admissibility.

first_actual_full_report.report:
Codex PASS lacked valid task or source evidence for every premise. The argument proves the exact conditional auxiliary equivalence under the task’s antecedents. No external mathematical premise is needed. The task assumptions are quoted below and excluded from premises. This verdict does not establish unrestricted S09, the 41-question programme, or article readiness.

Ordinary order implies ideal inclusion in the stated direction at every real t>0. Using the convention that I(tu) tests local integrability of |f|² exp(-2tu), v≤u+C implies exp(-2tu)≤exp(2tC)exp(-2tv). Consequently, integrability for v implies integrability for u. Constants and smooth bounded functions preserve multiplier ideals because they multiply these weights by factors bounded above and below by positive constants. These statements follow directly from local integrability, without a preservation theorem for limits. Compactness and the finite upper bound of genuine canonical u also ensure that sufficiently negative constant translates of u provide competitors.

The min/max bounds are valid for both families. Put m=min F and M=max F. Every zero-obstacle competitor a gives an F-obstacle competitor a+m; every F-obstacle competitor v gives a zero-obstacle competitor v−M. The required order conditions survive constant translation, for both ordinary and ideal orders. Taking suprema and upper regularizations therefore gives q+m≤Q_F≤q+M and q+m≤R_F≤q+M. This reasoning does not assume that q itself belongs to either original competitor family. Ordinary-to-ideal inclusion gives Q_F≤R_F, so the bounds imply Q_F≤R_F≤Q_F+(M−m).

All regularization steps preserve these pointwise inequalities. For any raw supremum h and continuous finite G, (h+G)*=h*+G. Regularization is monotone, and h≤G implies h*≤G when G is continuous. In particular, Q_F,R_F≤F. The bounded-type inequalities are meaningful at poles: Q_F(x)=−∞ forces R_F(x)=−∞ through the upper bound, while R_F(x)=−∞ forces Q_F(x)=−∞ through Q_F≤R_F. No difference between two infinite values is taken; subtraction of the finite smooth F is legitimate everywhere.

The gauge sign is correct: θ_F+D(v−F)=θ+Dv for θ_F=θ+DF. Thus v↦v−F is a bijection between θ-psh and θ_F-psh functions, preserving genuineness and canonical representatives. It sends v≤F exactly to v−F≤0. It preserves ordinary order relative to u↦u−F, and the equality I(t(v−F))=I(tv), together with its analogue for u, preserves ideal order for every t>0. Hence the entire competitor families correspond, not merely selected competitors. Commutation with continuous subtraction establishes Q_F−F=P_{θ_F}[u_F] and R_F−F=P_{θ_F}[u_F]_I. Closedness, positivity, or a cohomology class for θ is unnecessary.

Write q_F=Q_F−F and r_F=R_F−F. Both are genuine canonical θ_F-psh and lie below zero. To prove the ordinary model property of r_F, take any ordinary zero-obstacle competitor w for r_F. Then w+F is θ-psh, lies below F, and satisfies w+F≤R_F+C. Ordinary-to-ideal inclusion and the explicitly granted preservation antecedent give I(t(w+F))⊆I(tR_F)⊆I(tu) for every real t>0. Therefore w+F belongs to the defining ideal family for R_F, so w≤r_F. The raw supremum of these w is bounded by r_F; since r_F is upper semicontinuous, its upper regularization remains bounded by r_F, including at poles. Conversely, r_F itself is an ordinary competitor with constant C=0. Thus P_{θ_F}[r_F]=r_F. Preservation of the ideal envelope is used exactly here and is not inferred from an unsupported limiting argument.

Ordinary-type invariance also follows directly from the families. The bounds give q_F≤r_F≤q_F+d, where d=M−m is finite. A function bounded above by q_F+C is bounded above by r_F+C; one bounded above by r_F+C is bounded above by q_F+(d+C). Thus the ordinary zero-obstacle competitor families for q_F and r_F are identical, including at poles. It follows that P_{θ_F}[q_F]=P_{θ_F}[r_F]=r_F. This identity also establishes genuineness and canonical regularity of the iterated envelope without an additional assumption.

Both directions now follow. If Q_F=R_F, then q_F=r_F and P_{θ_F}[q_F]=q_F. Conversely, if P_{θ_F}[q_F]=q_F, the established identity P_{θ_F}[q_F]=r_F forces q_F=r_F, hence Q_F=R_F. Substituting q_F=P_{θ_F}[u_F] gives exactly the requested equivalence. The case M=m is included, and no division by M−m occurs.

Two harmless wording clarifications apply. Under the exp(-2φ) convention for multiplier ideals, replace t by 2t in the draft’s exponential comparison; under the exp(-φ) convention it is already correct. Also, ‘all-obstacle equality at this F’ means equality for this fixed obstacle. An all-F consequence requires the antecedents and transported idempotence for every relevant F. Neither clarification requires a new argument.

The [preprint lead](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12797v1) remains unverified as a theorem source for this audit and contributes no mathematical premise.
